title: Costs rebuild 2 · piece 5: opencode and runner-kit post per-request records
description:
**Piece 5 of LIN-4195** (D12). It needs piece 1 deployed and is independent of pieces 2–4. Until a lineage has records it reads from snapshots, by D7.

**opencode (runner,** `opencode-runner.js`**):**

* Build one record per assistant message from `GET /session/:id/message`, which is already read at \~`:958`/`:1486`.
  * `requestId` = the message id;
  * native `costUsd`;
  * the same five token fields as `postUsageFeedback` maps today (no 1h split);
  * `agent: 'main'`.
* Post them through the same ledger and resend mechanism as piece 2. Reuse it; do not fork it.
* Post from the normal end, the error path and the hold path (L8).

**runner-kit (Harbour,** `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs`**,** `usage` **command):**

* Post its subagent transcript's requests as records, through the runner-token route, using the same per-message walk (per-field max per `message.id`, skipping `<synthetic>` and zero-token messages).
* The orchestrator-tokens gap (L9) is named and left. Say so in the PR.
* `docs/runner-prompt.md` (\~:180-190, `runner usage <agentId>`) describes the cumulative `[usage]` line. Add the record post next to it; piece 6 removes the snapshot wording.

**Witnesses:**

* An opencode session fixture's records sum to the oracle, with native `costUsd` carried through.
* Re-posting changes nothing server-side.
* An error-path session still posts.
* runner-kit's records for a fixture transcript sum to the oracle.

**Acceptance:**

* The witnesses pass.
* Existing opencode and runner-kit snapshot posting is unchanged (piece 6 removes it).
* If piece 4 chose per-harness cutover scoping, confirm an opencode lineage moves to records cleanly. If it chose the control instead, confirm no live lineage mixes harnesses.

---

**Parent:** LIN-4195 "Costs rebuild 2: one record per model request, summed". Its full design (decisions D1–D14, the replay change list, the witnesses, the order of landing) is in LIN-4195's description under "## Implementation Plan". The plan-review notes are in LIN-4195's comment `eedab867-0fe0-4b15-b74a-2b78240f11d1`. The numbered notes cited here ("review note N") refer to that comment.

Session fit: fits one session
Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4195's approving plan-review (comment eedab867-0fe0-4b15-b74a-2b78240f11d1, rev 1)
Grounding commits: Harbour (JKershaw/LinearViewer) `72305215`, runner (JKershaw/simple-dispatcher) `cc2650a`. At breakdown (2026-11-04 \~01:45Z) neither repo had a commit after these.

The parent's approved plan is this piece's starting point; read it in full in LIN-4195's description. Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4195.

---

**Implemented (close-out, 2026-11-04):** as approved in LIN-4195's plan, no deviations. Harbour PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2266](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2266>) (`5334c81a`) and runner PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/315](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/315>) (`765289d4`). Full pre-close description is preserved in the task snapshots; the history is in the comment trail (see the `## Close-out — LIN-4202` comment for the live checks still to run).

comments.body:
## LIN-4202 (LIN-4195 piece 5): two PRs open, CI green on both, not merged

The ticket spans two repos, so there is one PR per repo. They link to each other.

| Repo | PR | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Harbour (runner-kit) | https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2266 | `7e38a3ca1101ece9f49c4a12582a931b183a5bc6` |
| runner (opencode) | https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/315 | `ea99dc4fd6e05203fbba7955669121eaabb6a256` |

**CI on those heads**
- **#2266** (run 41776718575): `Unit tests` ✅, `E2E shard 1/4`–`4/4` ✅, `Secret scan (source)` ✅, `CI success` ✅.
- **#315** (run 41777963909): `unit tests` ✅ (Linux, Node 22: 3982 tests, 3975 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped; the macOS-only suites skip themselves off-darwin).

### What was built
**Harbour: runner-kit `usage` command** (`lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs`)
- `foldTranscriptMessages`: the per-message, per-field max fold, moved out of `sumTranscriptUsage` so the snapshot and the records share it.
- `transcriptRequestRecords`: one record per request.
  - It is keyed by `message.id`, falling back to the line's top-level `requestId` (review note 8). A line with neither is skipped and counted.
  - It skips `<synthetic>` messages, even with non-zero tokens, and all-zero messages.
  - `agent` is the subagent id.
- `postRequestRecords`: posts to `POST /api/proxy/runner/usage/:id` in batches of ≤100. A 404 stops; a 5xx is reported and the other batches still go; it never throws.
- The command posts the records after the unchanged `[usage]` snapshot, and its JSON output gains a `records` summary.
- Docs: `docs/runner-prompt.md:180-183` and the source-map entry.

**Runner: opencode**
- `opencode-request-records.js` (new, pure): one record per assistant message of `GET /session/:id/message`:
  - `requestId` is `info.id`;
  - native `costUsd` is carried through;
  - the snapshot's four token fields, with no 1h field;
  - `harness: 'opencode'`, `agent: 'main'`, `lane: 'openrouter'`;
  - zero-token, non-assistant and id-less messages are skipped.
- `opencode-runner.js` `relayRequestRecords`: one bounded (10s) message-list read, gated on `WORKER_USAGE_RELAY`, called at five sites. Each posts **before** its terminal marker:
  - normal end, after the sentinel turn;
  - the not-clean turn;
  - each hold beat, reusing the beat's own read and posting to the live, repointed item;
  - the no-progress park;
  - the hard failure.

  Before this, the error and hold paths posted no `[usage]` at all, so this is new coverage (L8).
- Posting goes through **LIN-4199's ledger and resend** (#314, merged mid-task), reused, not forked.

### For the reviewer: shared code changed in LIN-4199's modules
1. **`request-usage-flush.js`.** I moved the batch, POST and ledger loop out of `flushRequestUsage` unchanged into `postRecordsWithLedger`. `flushRequestUsage` (claude-code, via `toWireRecord`) and the new `flushOpencodeRequestRecords` both call it.
   - The opencode poster posts records as they are. It does not use `toWireRecord`, which hardcodes `harness: 'claude-code'` and `costUsd: null`.
   - It uses the same `session.requestLedger`, keyed on the SD session id, committed through the runner's `updateStateFn` only after a 200.
   - The one new option is `stopOnNotTaken`, opencode only: a 404 skips the remaining batches. The claude-code flush still tries every batch; a new test pins that.
   - LIN-4199's own 47 tests pass before and after.
2. **`request-usage.js` `fingerprintOf`.** A finite `costUsd` now joins the hash, so a **cost-only change re-sends**. A message read on the error path can be partial. The cost is appended only when finite, so every claude-code record hashes exactly as before and no live ledger entry changes. 27 claude-code fingerprints recorded at `9478e1c` are pinned in `test/fixtures/opencode-session/claude-code-fingerprints-golden.json`.
3. **`opencode-runner.test.js` T1** now pins `workerUsageRelay: false`. It tests the tool-telemetry flag adding no fetches, and the records read belongs to the usage flag. This is the same pin LIN-3234 added to the sibling harness.

### Witnesses
**Harbour**
- `tests/unit/lin-4202-runner-kit-records.test.js`, 24 tests:
  - piece 0's 8 single-file stages: the records equal piece 0's and sum to the oracle within 1e-9;
  - per-field max on non-monotone lines;
  - a non-zero `<synthetic>` message produces no record;
  - the note-8 fallback;
  - batching 100/100/50, 404 stops, 5xx continues;
  - re-posting is idempotent against the **real** `postUsage` and store on MangoDB, and a grown transcript raises the total to the later oracle;
  - the snapshot fold equals a golden recorded from the unmodified function at `9cc5ff9c`.
- `tests/unit/runner-kit-helper.test.js`, +2 command tests: the snapshot post is unchanged with records beside it, and a 500 or 404 from the records route leaves the snapshot and the command result alone.
- Mutations, **10/10 caught:** last-line-wins, no synthetic skip, no `requestId` fallback, made-up id, no zero skip, 404 continues, batch size 200, failed batch throws, snapshot post dropped, records not posted.

**Runner**
- `test/lin-4202-opencode-records.test.js`, 34 tests. The real-poster tests use a fake intake at the fetch boundary with Harbour's semantics (per-field max upsert, zero-token not stored, 404 unless taken, 400 over 100). Harbour's real intake is in the other repo; #2266 proves it on MangoDB.
  - **Oracle through the real poster:** 4 documents, native cost 0.042, and token sums equal to the hand-written oracle in `test/fixtures/opencode-session/messages.json`.
  - **Re-posting changes nothing server-side:** the ledger sends nothing on a later site, and with the ledger deleted a full re-send leaves the store deep-equal.
  - **An error-path session still posts:** hard failure, park, the not-clean turn and the unclean hold beat each land the oracle before their `[failed]`/`[stalled?]`.
  - **5xx resend:** 250 requests, the second of 3 batches answered 500; 150 are acknowledged and the next flush sends only the missing 100.
  - **404 stops:** one POST, nothing acknowledged.
  - **Snapshot unchanged:** the golden recorded from the unchanged runner at `b6fc9ab` across all six scenarios is reproduced, apart from the one added records read.
- Mutations: **M1–M17 caught** (records mapping, the five sites, relay never throws, flag gate, read bound, live addressing, order before `[failed]`, snapshot payload). **W1–W13 caught** (default poster unwired in either deps block, `toWireRecord` used, ledger not consulted or not committed, 404 does not stop, stop-on-404 for claude-code, cost always or never in the fingerprint, state seams dropped, non-200 acknowledged, site removed, poster throws).
  - Survivors I fixed by strengthening tests: M2 (role filter), M13 (the read-bound test hung; it now fails in 10s), W2 (the hold's own default), W7 (claude-code 404 pin).

**Local runs on the final heads, using CI's invocations**
- Harbour: `test:hermetic:keyed` and `test:hermetic:proxy` (`CLOCK_SHIFT_DAYS=400`, local mongod) each 22958 pass, 0 fail; `secret-scan` pass.
- Runner: `npm test` 3991 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.
- Not run locally: Playwright E2E (CI ran it, green). Local Node is 25; CI uses 24 for Harbour and 22 for the runner.

### Left, and still open
- **Orchestrator-tokens gap (L9): named and deliberately left.** runner-kit records only each subagent's transcript; the orchestrating runner session's own tokens are not recorded.
- **Snapshot posting is unchanged** in both repos. Piece 6 (LIN-4203) removes it.
- **Prompt-size budget:** `docs/runner-prompt.md` is 17634 bytes against a 17638-byte ceiling. 4 bytes of headroom remain; the next edit must raise the ceiling with its reason.
- **Piece-4 cutover-scoping check: open.** LIN-4201 is still Todo. If it picks per-harness scoping, confirm an opencode lineage moves to records cleanly; if it picks the control, confirm no live lineage mixes harnesses. Until piece 4 switches the read, opencode lineages read from snapshots (D7).
- **Live check after deploy:** no opencode session has run against harbour.cat with this code. The first one should show `request-usage.flush` oplog lines with reason `opencode-*` and `request-usage` documents with `harness: 'opencode'`.

LIN-4202 stays **In Progress**. Merge and Done belong to review, then close-out.

## Autopilot run summary (stepper) — LIN-4202 implementation step

**Beats run (one warm session, ROOT 31638298):**
1. Ground + dependency check: found piece 2 (LIN-4199) had no code at HEAD; ruled `split` (runner-kit first, opencode pure function + unwired seam; no fork of piece 2).
2. runner-kit records walk + docs → LinearViewer PR #2266.
3. opencode records function + five relay sites behind a seam → simple-dispatcher PR #315.
4. Final CI-equivalent runs, push, open both PRs. LIN-4199 merged mid-beat; branch rebased onto it.
5. Ruled `wire-now` (ticket requires posting through piece 2's ledger): opencode poster on a shared ledger loop, real-poster witnesses.
6. CI confirmed on both PRs; worker summary posted (comment 218a2f6b).

**Evidence I checked myself:** commits present in the worker clones at each beat; both PRs open/mergeable; #2266 head 7e38a3ca — Unit tests, E2E 1–4, Secret scan, CI success all SUCCESS; #315 head ea99dc4 — `unit tests` SUCCESS.

**What holds:** records posted from runner-kit and opencode (normal end, not-clean turn, hold, park, hard failure); snapshot posting unchanged; mutation checks all caught.

**What's left / for review:** merge and Done are not done (review → close-out). Reviewer attention: edits to LIN-4199's shared flush loop/fingerprint (cost-only resend; claude-code fingerprints pinned by golden); piece-4 cutover scoping check still open (LIN-4201 Todo); L9 orchestrator-tokens gap deliberately left; first live opencode session after deploy should be checked; 4 bytes of headroom under the runner prompt size ceiling.

## Review — LIN-4202

Reviewed two heads: Harbour **#2266** head `7e38a3ca1101ece9f49c4a12582a931b183a5bc6`, and runner **#315** head `ea99dc4fd6e05203fbba7955669121eaabb6a256`. Both are open, MERGEABLE, and 0 commits behind `main`.

CI: green on both heads. #2266: Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan, CI success all SUCCESS. #315: `unit tests` SUCCESS. I also ran the tests myself on each PR head: runner `lin-4202` + `request-usage*` + `opencode-runner` tests, 287/287 pass. Harbour `lin-4202-runner-kit-records` + `runner-kit-helper`, 249/249 pass.

### Scope vs plan
The diff matches the plan and the implementation comment (218a2f6b). The work stayed inside the places the plan named. It also touches LIN-4199's shared modules, and the comment says so up front:
- the loop was moved out into `postRecordsWithLedger`;
- `fingerprintOf` now adds `costUsd` when it is finite.

That is a reuse, not a fork, which is what the ticket asks for. The ruling `lin4202-wire-after-4199` (wire-now) is resolved and was followed.

Wording note, not a defect: the ticket says "the same five token fields as `postUsageFeedback`". `postUsageFeedback` actually maps four (`opencode-runner.js:599-602`). With "no 1h split", four is correct, and that is what the implementation sends.

### Requirements check
- **opencode, one record per assistant message:** `opencode-request-records.js`. `requestId` = `info.id`, native `costUsd`, the snapshot's token mapping, `agent:'main'`. ✔
- **Posted through LIN-4199's ledger and resend:** `flushOpencodeRequestRecords` → `postRecordsWithLedger`, using the same `sessions[sdSessionId].requestLedger`. ✔
- **Posted on normal end, error path and hold path:** the relay sits at normal-end `:1603`, not-clean `:1775`, hold-beat `:1012`, park `:1850` and hard failure `:1878`. Each one runs before its terminal marker. ✔
- **runner-kit:** `transcriptRequestRecords` shares the per-field-max fold with the snapshot, skips `<synthetic>` and zero-token messages, and posts through `POST /api/proxy/runner/usage/:id` in batches of ≤100. The `[usage]` snapshot is posted first and is unchanged. ✔
- **Docs:** `docs/runner-prompt.md:180-183`. ✔
- **L9 named and left:** stated in the #2266 body. ✔
- **Snapshots unchanged:** pinned by goldens on both sides. The runner golden is from `b6fc9ab`, the Harbour golden from `9cc5ff9c`. ✔

### Regression check
- `git log` for `opencode-runner.js`, `request-usage*.js` and `runner.mjs` shows nothing reverted. LIN-4199 (`9478e1c`) behaviour holds:
  - its tests pass;
  - the claude-code flush still tries every batch on a 404 (the new W7 test pins this);
  - claude-code fingerprints are pinned by `claude-code-fingerprints-golden.json`.
- The usage-relay default (LIN-4127 `600f1be`) is respected: the records relay is gated on the same `WORKER_USAGE_RELAY` flag.
- The bounded-read idiom (LIN-3228) is followed: the records read has its own 10s abort.

### Mutation check (my own, each reverted)
- **Runner, 7/7 went red:**
  - hard-failure relay off: 2 fail;
  - hold-beat relay removed: 3 fail;
  - `costUsd` dropped: 10 fail;
  - park relay off: 2 fail;
  - ledger never committed: 3 fail;
  - fingerprint ignores cost: 1 fail;
  - normal-end relay removed: 3 fail.
- **Harbour, 5/5 went red:**
  - synthetic skip removed: 1;
  - records not posted: 2;
  - last-line-wins instead of max: 2;
  - 404 continues: 1;
  - `agent` dropped: 1.

### Cross-repo contract (checked here)
The runner tests use a fake intake. To check the real one, I fed `opencodeRequestRecords(test/fixtures/opencode-session/messages.json)` through Harbour's real `validateUsageBody` (`lib/request-usage-intake.js`). All 4 records were applied and 4 stored, with 0 rejected. `harness:'opencode'`, `lane:'openrouter'`, `costUsd`, the ISO `at` and `agent:'main'` are all accepted. `costUsd` is in the store's `$max` `GROWING_FIELDS`, so native cost persists. The wire shape is discharged against the fixture; real opencode output is covered by ledger item 1.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "harnesses that post `[usage]` snapshots and must also post per-request records". The `[usage]` producers are:
- `hook.js:453`, claude-code: LIN-4199, Done;
- `opencode-runner.js:608`, opencode: this PR;
- `runner.mjs` `usage`, runner-kit: this PR.

D12 bounds the class to these. No unhandled instance remains. The orchestrator-tokens gap (L9) is **outside**: the plan excluded it by name.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **[inside — D12 opencode] A live opencode session posts records.** CI only drives a fake intake and a hand-written message fixture. **After the deploy:** run the first opencode dispatch on harbour.cat with `SD_WORKER_USAGE_RELAY` on, and confirm all of:
  - SD's oplog has `request-usage.flush` with reason `opencode-normal-end`, and `posted>0`, `failed:0`;
  - `request-usage` has documents with `harness:'opencode'`, non-null `costUsd`, under the lineage's `rootItemId`;
  - their `costUsd` sum equals that run's `[usage]` snapshot `costUsd`, within 1e-9.

  The precondition that tells right from wrong is a run with ≥2 assistant messages, so a fold or role-filter error would show up as a mismatch.
- **[inside — D12 opencode error and hold paths] Error-path reads return the session's messages on a real server.** CI cannot reproduce a real opencode server just after a hard-bound abort. **Named monitor:** on an opencode `[failed]`, `[stalled?]` or hold-beat run, look for SD oplog `request-usage.flush` with reason `opencode-error-hard-failure`, `opencode-error-no-progress-park` or `opencode-hold-beat`. A miss shows up as the runner log line `request records (<site>) not posted (best-effort)`. Only production produces a real hung or aborted server, which is why no earlier check can prove this.
- **[inside — D12 runner-kit] A live person-run runner posts records.** The kit is served with a sha256 pin, so this needs a runner that fetched the new kit. **After the deploy:** on one `runner usage <agentId>`, confirm both:
  - the JSON shows `records.found>0`, `records.posted == records.found`, `notTaken:false`, `failedBatches:0`;
  - `request-usage` documents carry `agent:<agentId>` and `harness` = the kit's harness, under the row's anchor.
- **[inside — acceptance, piece-4 cutover scoping] Not dischargeable yet.** LIN-4201 is Todo and has not chosen between per-harness scoping and the mixed-harness control (piece 0's `1b6c6758`). Merging is safe without it: nothing reads records yet, and D7 keeps opencode lineages on snapshots. **After the deploy, and after LIN-4201 lands:**
  - if LIN-4201 chose per-harness scoping: confirm that one opencode lineage with records reads its cost from records, and that the cost equals its snapshot sum;
  - if it chose the control: confirm no live lineage mixes `harness` values across its `request-usage` documents.

  Close-out may merge on the other items. LIN-4202 should not move to **Done** until this check runs, or until the human explicitly drops it with a reason. Filing a ticket does not discharge it.
- **[inside] Deploy order.** opencode records rely on piece 1 (LIN-4198) being live on harbour.cat. If the runner deploys first, `/api/dispatch/usage/:itemId` returns 404, `stopOnNotTaken` stops the posting quietly, and nothing is lost: a later flush resends whatever the ledger has not acknowledged. **Before the merge:** confirm LIN-4198 is deployed on harbour.cat.
- **Rollback (named):** revert the squash-merge commit of #315 (runner) and/or #2266 (Harbour). No migration is involved, and the records written are additive (nothing reads them until piece 4), so the change is reversible while LIN-4201 is unmerged.

### Notes (no change needed)
- `docs/runner-prompt.md` has 4 bytes of headroom under its ceiling (17634/17638). The next prompt edit, piece 6, must raise the ceiling.
- The hard-failure path can now take up to 10s for the read, plus the flush budget, before `[failed]`. That is acceptable, and bounded by design.

### Verdict
**Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger.** Both PRs meet the D12 requirements and reuse LIN-4199's ledger. My own mutations (12/12) went red, and the opencode wire shape is accepted by Harbour's real intake. The open items are three live checks after the deploy, one deploy-order check, and the piece-4 scoping acceptance, which holds Done until LIN-4201 lands.

## Close-out — LIN-4202

**Merged (squash, each pinned with `--match-head-commit` to the head review approved):**
- Harbour #2266 → `5334c81a7207b9f2cc85ca429a2c6b18e1635c0e` (head `7e38a3ca`). Deployed: harbour.cat footer shows `5334c81a…`; main `Tests` run on that commit is green.
- runner #315 → `765289d46e42e757283e27e08fe56284cd6792eb` (head `ea99dc4f`). Runner is not a hosted deploy; it takes effect when an operator's runner pulls main and restarts. I cannot see that from here.

**CI:** green on the exact merged heads. #2266: Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan, CI success. #315: `unit tests`. Both PRs were `CLEAN`/`MERGEABLE` on a fresh read at merge time.

**Changes I made after approval:** none. Review asked for no fixes, so there is no unreviewed delta.

### Ledger
- **Deploy order (inside):** discharged. LIN-4198 (piece 1) merged as `9cc5ff9c` and the harbour.cat footer showed `9cc5ff9c…` before this merge, so the `/api/dispatch/usage/:itemId` and runner-token routes exist. Harbour then deployed `5334c81a`.
- **Live opencode session posts records (inside):** **not run.** It needs a real opencode dispatch with `SD_WORKER_USAGE_RELAY` on, plus the SD oplog and the `request-usage` store, and I have neither. Runnable by the operator after their runner picks up `765289d`: check the SD oplog for `request-usage.flush` reason `opencode-normal-end` with `posted>0, failed:0`; check `request-usage` docs for `harness:'opencode'` and non-null `costUsd`, summing to the run's `[usage]` snapshot `costUsd` within 1e-9. Use a run with ≥2 assistant messages.
- **Error and hold path reads on a real server (inside):** **not run**, same access. Named monitor, as review wrote it: oplog `request-usage.flush` with reason `opencode-error-hard-failure`, `opencode-error-no-progress-park` or `opencode-hold-beat`. A miss shows as the runner log line `request records (<site>) not posted (best-effort)`.
- **Live runner-kit post (inside):** **not run.** It needs a person-run runner that has fetched the new sha256-pinned kit. Operator check: on one `runner usage <agentId>`, the JSON shows `records.found>0`, `posted == found`, `notTaken:false`, `failedBatches:0`, and `request-usage` docs carry `agent:<agentId>`.
- **Piece-4 cutover-scoping acceptance (inside):** **not run, and cannot run yet.** LIN-4201 is still Todo and has not picked per-harness scoping or the mixed-harness control. Nothing reads records yet, and D7 keeps opencode lineages on snapshots, so the merge is safe. I have noted the check on LIN-4201 so it is carried there. Review asked that Done wait for this check. Close-out rules say a post-deploy check I cannot run does not hold the close, so I closed. The check is **not** discharged, and the operator should treat it as open.
- **Rollback (named by review):** revert squash commit `765289d4` (runner) and/or `5334c81a` (Harbour). No migration is involved and the records are additive, so this is clean while LIN-4201 is unmerged.
- **L9 orchestrator-tokens gap (outside):** named in the PR and left by plan. Nothing filed: the plan excluded it by name.
- **Prompt-size headroom (note):** `docs/runner-prompt.md` has 4 bytes under its ceiling (17634/17638). LIN-4203 (piece 6) must raise the ceiling with its reason.

**Not run, for the operator (what / why / who):** the three live checks above (opencode normal-end, opencode error/hold, runner-kit) need production access to the SD oplog and the Harbour store. The piece-4 scoping check needs LIN-4201 to land first. All four are to be run by the operator.

**Follow-ups filed:** none. Every open item is inside work or a live check, not an outside problem. Related tickets: LIN-4203 stays Todo (blocked-by this, now unblocked); LIN-4201 got a note carrying the scoping check; LIN-4195 stays In Progress (pieces 3, 4, 6 open).

**Archive and prune:** a pre-prune snapshot exists (`b7273e0a…`, captured 2026-11-04T05:23:36Z, carrying the full description). The description holds only the problem statement, scope, witnesses and acceptance (the plan lives on LIN-4195), so nothing was removed. I appended an implemented-by stub.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was it difficult?** The runner-kit half wasn't; its only friction was 4 bytes of prompt-size headroom and piece 1's census test. The opencode half was hard for two reasons:
- **The dependency moved under me.** Piece 2's ledger didn't exist at the start, so I built behind an unwired seam. LIN-4199 then merged during beat 4, and I had to rebase and rewire.
- **`opencode-runner.js` was where it bound.** It's ~1900 lines with five end paths, each with its own addressing (launch-frozen or live-repointed). `base` and `sessionId` were scoped to `try`, invisible to the catch, and there were ordering rules (post before the terminal marker, the LIN-3208 race notes).
- **Reusing LIN-4199 meant pushing through its claude-code assumptions:** `toWireRecord` hardcodes the harness and a null cost, the fingerprint ignored cost, and the post loop sat inside a transcript-reading function. I extracted it rather than calling it.
- **The tests fought back too.** A non-injectable `setInterval` made one mutation hang the test process.

**2. First.** Ask about ordering. "Independent of pieces 2–4" and "reuse piece 2's ledger" can't both hold, and the breakdown edge took the first reading. I'd have sequenced piece 5 after piece 2, or asked piece 2 to land its poster as a harness-neutral module.

**3. Tidy:**
- Fold opencode's five end-path call sites into one session-end function, so records, the `[usage]` delta and the terminal marker happen in one ordered place.
- Drop `stopOnNotTaken` and let claude-code stop on a 404 too. I kept it divergent only to avoid changing LIN-4199 unasked.
- Make the permission-stall interval injectable.
- Settle one token-field vocabulary (opencode maps four, claude-code five).

**4. The ideal ticket.** A harness-neutral usage-records module would exist: adapters turn native output into records, with one poster and ledger behind them. This ticket would be "add the opencode adapter (pure) and register it at session end": about 60 lines and a fixture. runner-kit, a self-contained kit in another repo, would still walk on its own, but share the record shape.

**5. What it got wrong:**
- The dependency on piece 2 was stated as independence.
- "Already read at `:1486`": that read is off by default and runs before the sentinel turn.
- The error and hold paths were framed as extra places to post. They posted no `[usage]` at all, so L8 was a gap, not a duplicate.
- "Five token fields" for opencode; there are four.
- "The same per-message walk" glossed over runner-kit's fold counting each id-less line as its own message.
- The piece-4 cutover confirmation couldn't be done here, because piece 4 hadn't decided.
